verdicts.quote: “Slack apps are installed with a v2 OAuth 2.0 flow.”
verdicts.reason: Official auth docs state OAuth 2.0 is the install/auth mechanism Slack apps use.

verdicts.quote: “Click Activate Public Distribution. Once distribution is enabled, you’ll get access to an embeddable Add to Slack button [and] a shareable URL that kicks off the installation process…”
verdicts.reason: This shows developers can self-serve app credentials and distribution without prior review; Marketplace listing is only needed for commercial directory distribution.

verdicts.quote: “With over 200 methods, surely there’s one right for you. You can find them all in the reference…”
verdicts.reason: Slack exposes hundreds of Web API methods plus Events, Admin, Audit, SCIM, etc., indicating broad API surface.

verdicts.quote: “We’re excited to announce… the Slack Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and the Real-time Search (RTS) API!”
verdicts.reason: The MCP server is announced on Slack’s official developer changelog; Slack also later announced a Slackbot MCP Client.

verdicts.quote: “The rate limits for… `conversations.history` and `conversations.replies`… will be limited to 1 request per minute… [and] the… `limit`… reduced to 15 objects [for] apps… not approved for the Slack Marketplace.”
verdicts.reason: Buildable now, but there are caveats: non‑Marketplace commercial apps face stricter rate limits on message history, and some APIs (e.g., SCIM) are plan‑gated to Business+/Enterprise, so an agent toolkit would need to account for these constraints.
